root_cause_proof: Both lifetimes() and snapshot() enumerate proc_listallpids(): every UID is included, except zero/self filtering, and neither source path first filters candidate ownership in the kernel.
Both then call _basic(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO=3) before checking info.uid; the requested full BSD information is privileged across different effective UIDs.

Apple XNU proc_pidinfo leaves PROC_PIDTBSDINFO in CHECK_SAME_USER. proc_security_policy compares effective UIDs and returns EPERM to an ordinary caller lacking PRIV_GLOBAL_PROC_INFO for a foreign target.

The public libproc wrapper converts the failing syscall to returned size0 while errno remains EPERM. _basic only treats ESRCH/ENOENT as absence, so the intended later info.uid filter is unreachable for a denied foreign PID.
Thus a live ordinary foreign-UID process creates a deterministic preflight failure and can also stop worker-cleanup inventory even though that process is outside ownership scope.

Backend construction already completed its own-process full BSD/path/audit-token capability check in the hosted execution. This counters the assumption that every identity API or the 136-byte layout was universally unusable.

implemented_in_draft: Bind public proc_listpids(uint32_t,uint32_t,void*,int) with ctypes c_int return and select PROC_UID_ONLY=4 plus os.geteuid().
Validate byte-return units, minimum whole PID record, divisibility and maximum4096 records with4097-slot allocation; a full/truncated allocation is failure.
Reject malformed negative/duplicate PID records rather than silently normalizing them. Continue excluding kernel PID0 and current process from worker candidates.

Retain all existing per-candidate UID, original lifetime, start-boundary, executable, tracking marker, full audit-token and token-bound signal checks. No global scan, elevated permission, PID/PGID fallback, or blanket EPERM suppression.

Capture numeric errno immediately and report only numeric PID/size/expected-size/returned-PID/errno (inventory also numeric UID/capacity). No executable/environment/tracking contents are added to diagnostics.

counter_evidence_and_alternatives: A disappearing PID already maps ESRCH/ENOENT to None; blanket skip-on-any-error would instead hide genuine same-UID candidate ownership failures and is explicitly not the fix.

Short BSD-info is publicly readable but lacks the full start-time proof; using an extra short-record UID probe is more complex than kernel UID selection and does not justify weakening the full identity checks.
A broken struct/API could also produce the old generic exception, but own-process capability passed. Numeric diagnostics preserve future distinctions without asserting the unrecorded hosted errno.

The old37 synthetic Apple tests covered high-level mocked Workers, tokens and simulator controls but did not exercise _pids/_basic/lifetimes process-enumeration privilege ordering; their earlier green result is not native evidence.
Do not remove the failing cleanup outcome checks: they are expected propagation of failed preflight and not proof that actual build outputs leaked.
